instruction.name: x86settm
instruction.description: Set the x87 translation mode, enabling TOP-based remapping of the FPRs.

throughput.name: 16 instructions per body
throughput.asm: x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm
throughput.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 2000 --unroll2 8000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'li.d $r12, 5' --asm 'x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm; x86settm; x86clrtm'
throughput.notes: Enabling the translation mode breaks the epilogue of the surrounding function, so the instruction cannot be measured alone: the pair `x86settm; x86clrtm` takes 14.00 cycles and `x86clrtm` alone 7.00, which puts `x86settm` at 7 as well.

notes: Enabling the translation mode breaks the epilogue of the surrounding function, so the instruction cannot be measured alone: the pair `x86settm; x86clrtm` takes 14.00 cycles and `x86clrtm` alone 7.00, which puts `x86settm` at 7 as well. The instruction has no register operands, so no latency entry can be attached to one; the chain is over internal x87 state.
